title: Key transit routes
steps: Tokyo → Yamagata: Yamagata Shinkansen "Tsubasa" direct from Tokyo Station, ≈2h22m fastest (up to ≈2h45m), roughly hourly. Every seat is reserved — book all 8 together. ⚠ ≈¥11,450 one-way reserved seat, corroborated via two independent fare-table sites, not JR East's own page (bot-gated this pass) — confirm at booking.

Yamagata → Yamadera: JR Senzan Line direct, ≈19-23 min, roughly hourly. ⚠ ≈¥260 cash / ≈¥253 IC one-way, corroborated via aggregator only — confirm at the station. Yamadera Station is a ≈10 min walk from Risshaku-ji's base entrance.

Yamagata → Oishida (for Ginzan Onsen): JR Ōu Line — local train ≈50 min, or Tsubasa ≈28 min (extra limited-express surcharge). Suica/IC cards are not usable at Ōishida Station per multiple Japanese sources (not confirmed against JR East directly) — buy a paper ticket.

Oishida → Ginzan Onsen (the anchor transfer, carried with luggage): Hanagasa Bus, Ginzan Line, ≈35-40 min, ¥1,000/adult one-way, cash only, no reservation needed. Confirmed running Apr 1 – Oct 24, 2026 (covers the trip). Only 5-6 buses/day (sample departures 6:40/9:57/12:42/14:17/16:02/17:52 from Oishida) — missing one means a 1.5-2.5h wait. Board early with the group's luggage; if the bus can't take it all, a taxi (≈20 min, ≈¥6,500-8,000/car, 2-3 cars for 8 people — call Ōbanazawa Taxi 0237-23-2525 ahead) is the fallback.
Ginzan Onsen → Oishida (return): last practical bus back is ≈17:04 if attempting this as a day trip. On the overnight plan, any of the 6 daily departures works for the return leg.
Getting around Yamagata city: the station area is walkable (most central hotels are 5-8 min on foot), with a taxi rank and bus terminal directly outside the station.
